about: The tool descriptions as main held them before the ASD-STE100 rewrite (branch explore/full-ste); scripts/ste_check.py compares with them. toolNames: every tool name of this add-on, Agent Link and its other add-ons, to find the ones a text points to.

texture_list.description: The texture library Texturizer ships (BumpMesh's, by Stefan Hermann, CNC Kitchen): for each texture its id, name, category (geometric, patterns, organic, fabric, natural, grip, mold, tires; custom for your own PNGs), credit, licence, source_url and defaults (scaleU: the tile in mm on a 50 mm part; the draft scales it to the part). Inputs: category (one of those names; a wrong one is refused with the list) and search (a part of the name, any case); both optional, both together narrow. Use an id as texture in texture_set or texture_apply. The reply: count, textures, categories, credit, note. Reads only; small and quick.

texture_settings.description: BumpMesh's settings as the engine takes them, and what a run on a body would cost. With no arguments: defaults (e.g. refineLength 1 mm, maxTriangles 750 000, textureHeight 0.5 mm, scaleU 25 mm), layerKeys (set per layer), globalKeys (set once for the run), mappingModes (0 planarXY, 1 planarXZ, 2 planarYZ, 3 cylindrical, 4 spherical, 5 triplanar, 6 cubic, 7 surfaceNormal, 8 outlineWrap), maxLayers (4), units and the credit. With body (a solid's name or label; left out with texture given: the document's one body) and optionally texture (a library id) and settings: body.size in mm, body.estimate at the settings' refineLength { edge, inputTriangles, subdividedTriangles, outputTriangles (capped at maxTriangles), memoryBytes (about 420 bytes per subdivided triangle), safetyCap }, body.suggest { refineLength, maxTriangles, pixelsPerEdge } (BumpMesh's Suggest values; only with texture) and body.cylinder (a fitted axis for cylindrical mapping). Call it before texture_apply on anything large: texture_apply refuses a run whose estimate is over 4 GB (about 10 million subdivided triangles), and halving refineLength makes about four times the triangles. tolerance: the body's tessellation in mm (0.02; the draft tools always use 0.02). Unknown setting names are refused. Reads only; the body is tessellated, which takes a moment on a part with many curved faces.

texture_draft.description: Start or read the texture draft: the one draft per window that the Texturizer sidebar shows and that texture_set, texture_mask, texture_layer, texture_preview and texture_apply work on. Call it first, with part. Inputs: part (or body: the same) — a solid's or a Mesh object's name or label; a Textured object (texture_apply's) brings back the settings it was made with and its body as the part, so the next texture_apply updates it. Left out, the draft keeps its part, or takes the one visible solid (several: refused with their names). reset: true is BumpMesh's Reset to defaults (done before part). draft: a whole draft object to load. project: a .bumpmesh file path (BumpMesh's Load Project; relative: the output folder), with mode all (settings and the file's model, added as a Mesh object and made the part) or settings; project "ask" opens a file dialog in the window and waits for a person, so give a path. load: "selection" takes the object selected in the window. layer is not used here. It opens the sidebar in the window (shown live, Agent Link brings the Texturizer workbench forward first); the model is not changed, and the draft is kept in the document (a hidden TextureDraft object), so Edit > Undo undoes draft edits. The reply: mesh { triangles, faces } (the part's tessellation at 0.02 mm; faces 0 for a Mesh part), draft { part, label, frame, active, settings (those changed from the defaults), canUndo, canRedo, layers: each layer (0 = bottom), name, texture, visible, solo, blend cover|add, mode include|exclude, faces (FaceN names), triangles masked, brush { split, soft } }, project { mode, warnings, note } after a load, and note with the next steps. Faces are the part's own Face1..FaceN (from 1); they renumber when the CAD model changes, and the draft follows them by FreeCAD's stable names or their surface. The engine and settings are BumpMesh's (Stefan Hermann, CNC Kitchen), ported. guide_read { topic: "texture" } has the whole workflow.

texture_set.description: Change the draft (texture_draft first): a partial update in one undo step; the sidebar's controls move as it runs. Inputs: layer (0 = bottom; the active one when left out); active (make this layer the one the sidebar edits, done first); texture — a library id (texture_list), or {"file": a PNG heightmap's path}, which is copied into your custom textures (setting a texture also resets scaleU / scaleV to the texture's tile scaled to the part, so give settings in the same call or after); settings by BumpMesh's names (texture_settings lists them): for the layer e.g. scaleU / scaleV (mm per tile; scaleV follows scaleU while lockScale is on), textureHeight (mm, the depth; the same control as amplitude, taken unsigned — invertDisplacement: true cuts in instead of standing out), mappingMode (0-8 or a name such as "cubic"), rotation (degrees, in the surface), and for the run refineLength (mm: the edge the mesh is refined to), maxTriangles (the result is reduced to it), bottomAngleLimit / topAngleLimit (degrees: faces flatter than this, facing down / up, stay plain); frame {rotation: [x, y, z] degrees (BumpMesh's Rotate: turns the texturing frame, not the body)}, frame {direction: [x, y, z]} (point a planar projection along it; not [0, 0, 0]) or frame {face: a face name or "selected"} (Place on Face); cylinder autofit | reset | from_face (with face: a cylindrical face's name) for cylindrical mapping; stamp "on" | "off" | {point, normal} (one tile placed at a spot; "place" uses a spot clicked in the window). A name that is not a setting, or an engine tuning setting the draft does not hold (those go in texture_apply's settings), is refused. {"upload": true} as texture and stamp "place" and face "selected" need a person at the window. The reply: layer, set (what was set, with the values the draft took after clamping) and draft (as texture_draft). The model is untouched: nothing is textured until texture_preview or texture_apply; the draft is kept in the document, so Edit > Undo undoes it.

texture_mask.description: Say where one layer's texture goes (BumpMesh's Masking); texture_draft first. mode exclude (the listed faces stay plain, the rest is textured; the default) or include (only the listed faces are textured); changing mode clears the layer's faces, as BumpMesh, so give mode before or with add. On a solid: add / remove faces by name ("Face3", a list, or a face query such as {"normal": [0, 0, 1]}; add: "selected" takes the faces picked in the window); add_by direction (faces facing within angle degrees, 10, of the faces given), box (faces inside their bounding box) or surface (faces on the same plane, cylinder, cone or sphere), each starting from faces; fill: seed faces or {faces, maxAngle} spreads across edges where the faces meet at under maxAngle degrees (20). On a Mesh part (no faces): triangles (indices from 0 of the part's tessellation; out of range is refused), fill {triangles: [seeds], maxAngle, erase} and paint. paint is BumpMesh's Brush on any part: strokes of hits in mm on the surface (see paint's own description), each stroke one undo step. clear: true empties the layer's mask (done before add in the same call). Order inside one call: mode, clear, add, triangles, remove, add_by, fill, then paint. Face names are the part's Face1..FaceN (from 1) as it is now: read them again after a CAD change (the draft's own masks follow the part by FreeCAD's stable names or surface). Name the faces that must not change (mating faces, press fits, threads) and say them back to the person first. The reply: layer, mode, faces (the layer's face names), triangles (source triangles masked by any means), brush {split, soft}, strokes, facesBrushedOff (faces a stroke took off the layer's list: mode standard paints or erases whole triangles of the part's tessellation, and a flat face of a solid is often only two), and note saying in words what gets textured. The model is untouched; the draft is kept in the document, so Edit > Undo undoes it.

texture_layer.description: The draft's layer strip (BumpMesh's; 1 to 4 layers, layer 0 is the bottom); texture_draft first. action: add (a copy of the active layer with an empty Include Only mask, made active: give it faces with texture_mask or it textures nothing; refused at 4); remove (the last one stays); move (delta -1 up the strip, +1 down; value is taken when delta is left out); solo (value true / false: only this layer in the preview; the export ignores solo); visible (value true / false: a hidden layer is left out of the preview and of texture_apply, which refuses when every layer is hidden); blend (value "cover": replaces the layers below where it applies, or "add": adds its depth to them; layer 0 always covers); name (value: text); active (the layer the sidebar edits and the other texture tools default to). layer: which one (the active one when left out; not used by add). The reply: draft (as texture_draft: every layer with its texture, mode, faces, blend and visibility). The model is untouched; the draft is kept in the document, so Edit > Undo undoes it.

texture_preview.description: Build the draft's preview with BumpMesh's engine (the same code as the export, so what shows is what prints), wait for it and show it in the 3D view in place of the part; texture_draft first. quality draft (a budget of 500 000 triangles; the default) or fine (1 500 000): the preview coarsens its own edge to fit that budget and 1 GB, so it never refuses for size, and previewEdge says how coarse it is against the export's edge. It can also be finer: BumpMesh's preview edge is at most the part's largest size / 80, so on a small part with a coarse refineLength the picture shows detail the result will not have; warnings then says so and names the refineLength that matches. The reply: part, quality, previewEdge (mm), triangles, vertices, inputTriangles, ms, export { edge, triangles, memoryMB } (what texture_apply would make at the draft's refineLength and maxTriangles: read it before applying; over 4096 MB texture_apply refuses), warnings and next. Other calls, each doing only that: suggest: true sets BumpMesh's Suggest values (refineLength and maxTriangles) in the draft for the active layer's texture and answers them, building nothing; cancel: true stops a preview the window is running, its pending rebuild timer cancelled and its worker thread waited for up to 2 s (note says so when it had not ended by then: its result is then dropped when it does), and answers window as texture_apply does (a built preview answers window too); turntable true / false starts or stops a slow spin of the 3D view about the part's vertical axis (15 degrees a second), and a number turns the view once by that many degrees for a series of renders (turn, view_snapshot, turn). layer is not used. It runs in its place, never as one of Agent Link's jobs (background: true is refused): it draws in the 3D view and starts and stops the preview's worker and timers, which only FreeCAD's window thread may do, so the call waits for the build (a fine preview of a large part takes longer; draft first). The wait has a time budget: wait seconds (default 45, at most 60); the worker does the maths and the window draws what it hands back (a coarse first look, then the result) as it comes. Past the budget the answer says building: true and verdict "still building", with how long it waited; the preview goes on building and shows in the 3D view when it is done, texture_preview {} again waits for that same build (it never starts a second one) and answers what it made, and cancel: true stops it. A preview already up to date for the draft answers at once (reused: true). The preview belongs to the draft's own document: it shows only while that document is in front, steps aside (the part shown again) when another document comes to the front or that document closes, and is taken out of the view when texture_apply or texture_export ends the sequence; the next draft tool brings it back. It changes nothing in the document (the preview is a view, and a save keeps the body shown). Look at it with view_snapshot; it says how it looks, texture_check (after texture_apply) says whether it is right.

texture_apply.description: Texture a part and put the result in the document (Add to document / Update / Bake Textures) with BumpMesh's engine (Stefan Hermann, CNC Kitchen), ported to Python and run inside FreeCAD. The result is a new Textured Mesh object beside the body; the body and its Shape are never changed, and the result is a mesh, not a solid: later CAD steps (fillets, holes, booleans) do not build on it, so texture last, then slice the mesh. Three ways to call it. (1) The draft: with no texture and no layers it textures the draft the sidebar shows (texture_draft, texture_set, texture_mask first; body switches the draft's part; draft loads a whole draft first) and makes the object, or updates the one this draft made before (new: true makes another; name labels it). (2) In one call, no draft: body, texture (a library id, texture_list), faces with mode include (texture only them: a grip) or exclude (keep them plain; the default; no faces: everything), settings by BumpMesh's names (textureHeight mm deep, scaleU mm per tile, mappingMode 0-8 or a name, refineLength mm, maxTriangles), rotation [x, y, z] degrees (BumpMesh's Rotate), or up to 4 layers, bottom first, each {texture, settings, faces, mode, blendAdd, visible}: a layer without its own texture, faces or mode takes the top-level one, one that differs from it is refused, and settings' layer settings are every layer's defaults. (3) update: a Textured object's name, run again now with what it stores; include_new: true also textures the faces a later CAD step made (they stay smooth until then). bake: true (draft only) is BumpMesh's Bake Textures: the undecimated result becomes the draft's part with a fresh layer, which with bakeMask on (the default) excludes what was just textured. export: a path ending .stl or .3mf (relative: the output folder), or {path, format}, writes the file as well. Following the body: an object made from the draft is linked to its body and textures it again by itself when the body changes (with the window: in the background, TextureState "updating…" meanwhile), its masks following the faces by FreeCAD's stable names or their surface; a mask that no longer fits is left out and reported (maskReport), never guessed. An object made the one-call way (2) is only marked OutOfDate when its body changes: run update. Face names are Face1..FaceN of the body as it is now (from 1); they renumber after CAD changes, so read them again before a one-call apply. Size and cost: this changes the document, so it cannot run as a job; it runs inside the call and FreeCAD's window is busy until it ends. The mesh is refined until no edge is longer than refineLength (1 mm by default; halving it makes about four times the triangles and the time), then reduced to maxTriangles (750 000 by default). A run estimated over memoryLimitGB (4, about 10 million refined triangles) is refused with what to raise; ask texture_settings { body, texture, settings } or texture_preview for the estimate first, and prefer a mask (only the faces that need texture) to a finer refineLength on a large part. tolerance (one-call way only): the body's tessellation in mm (0.02). The reply: body, object (the Textured object's name), label, updated, triangles, inputTriangles, repair, warnings (e.g. the subdivision hit its cap, so the texture is coarser than asked; open edges), layers (each with layer — its index from 0, bottom first, the number texture_mask, texture_set and texture_layer take — mode and faces; name and texture too when made from the draft), engine { refineLength, maxTriangles, subdivided, displaced, output, ms per stage }, credit, export { path, format, triangles }, state / maskReport / newFaces / included after an update, baked / maskedTriangles after a bake, next, and "health" from the shared check. As PartDesign hides the previous feature, the Body is hidden while its textured result is shown (its flat faces would show through; faces left smooth are part of the result mesh): bodyHidden true and the note say so; hiding or deleting the result, or Edit > Undo of the apply, shows the Body again. The preview, if one showed, is closed and switched off in its own document's view (the next draft tool brings it back on the body). With FreeCAD's window the answer has window: the document in front and the draft's (activeDocument, draftDocument, draftInFront), previewShowing, userHidden, the preview's nodes in the active view's scene graph and whether each is on (preview.scene.previewNodes), the result's and the body's eyes (result, source: visible, shown), and resultInView (whether the camera sees the result's box centre); and, to tell why a view with the result shown still draws nothing, resultView (the result's DisplayMode, Visibility, Transparency, facets, its RootNode and SwitchNode), camera (type, position, nearDistance, farDistance, focalDistance, height), scene (the active view's scene graph two levels deep: each node's type, name, children and whichChild, style, transparency, on, test) and viewer (the viewer's whole scene, two levels). A Texturizer bug that numpy refuses (an array in a truth test, a shape that does not fit) is refused with code failed and the file:line it came from. It opens no dialog or progress window. Then texture_check { object } measures the result against the body.

texture_export.description: Write a file. format stl or 3mf: with object (a Textured object's name) its mesh as it is, quick; without object the draft's part is textured by BumpMesh's engine straight into the file and nothing is added to the document (the same size limits as texture_apply: refused over memoryLimitGB, 4, with what to raise). format bumpmesh is BumpMesh's Save Project, which opens here or in the BumpMesh web app: the draft's settings and masks, the part's model unless model is false, your own textures unless texture is false. path: where (relative: the output folder; ~ is your home folder). Always give path, or ask: false for the default name in the output folder (<object label>.stl, <part label>_textured.stl, <part label>.bumpmesh): with neither, and FreeCAD's window open, a file dialog (for bumpmesh an options dialog too) opens and the call waits for a person. layer is not used. The reply: path, format, triangles, credit, warnings (an object that is out of date: update it with texture_apply first), object and next for an object's STL, files for a project; cancelled: true when a person closed the dialog. Run as one of Agent Link's jobs (past about 45 s, or background: true) it never opens a dialog, which only FreeCAD's window thread may: without path it writes to the default name in the output folder. 3MF and STL carry the credit (BumpMesh, CNC Kitchen). A long read when it runs the engine: it runs as a job, so past about 45 s the call answers with a job id and job_status gives the answer. An STL of a Textured object can be checked later with texture_check { path }.

texture_prepare.description: For texturing outside FreeCAD (the BumpMesh web app or its own tools): writes a body as one STL, face by face from one mesh of the whole part, and beside it <name>-mask.json listing the triangles of faces. To texture inside FreeCAD use texture_apply instead; this is not needed for it. Inputs: body (a solid's name or label; the document's one body when left out); faces (required: names such as "Face3", a list, or face queries; Face1..FaceN of the body as it is now); mode include (texture only them: a grip; the default) or exclude (all but them: keep a mating face plain); tolerance: the tessellation in mm (0.02; smaller means more triangles in the STL; give the same value to texture_check); path: the STL to write (relative: the output folder; default <label>-for-texture.stl there); name: a label for the default file name, not a path. The reply: body, stl, triangles, mask, maskTriangles, mode, faces, next (the bumpmesh_texture_file call to make with these files, a tool of the separate BumpMesh server, when it is connected) and note. The mask is tied to this tessellation: if the body changes, prepare again. Changes nothing in the document. Declared a long read (it runs as a job: past about 45 s the call answers with a job id and job_status gives the answer).

texture_check.description: Measure a textured mesh against the body it was made from, face by face, so a number and not a picture says whether the texture is right. object: a Textured object texture_apply made — its body, mask and angle limits come from what it stores and its own mesh is measured (or give only path: an STL texture_export wrote from it, matched to its object). For an STL textured outside FreeCAD: body, path and mask (texture_prepare's -mask.json; found beside path by name when left out), with the tolerance texture_prepare used (0.02), else it is refused because the triangle counts differ. Paths: relative means the output folder. flat: mm a point may move and still count as unmoved (0.01). reach: how far from the body a point is looked for, mm (the larger of 2 mm and 2 % of the body's diagonal; raise it for a texture deeper than that). The reply: verdict "ok" or "check"; texturedFaces (per face meant for texture: points, moved (the share that moved, 0-1), mean, p95, out, into, in mm); depth (the deepest, mm); leaked { faces, points, worst } — faces meant to stay plain that moved (a mating face, a datum): fix the mask and texture again; bare — faces meant for texture where under a fifth of the points moved (the texture is finer than refineLength, or the mask missed them); angleMasked — faces BumpMesh's bottom / top angle limits cover whole (they stay plain by design; a part's flat underside is one); far — points farther than reach; mesh { openEdges, overSharedEdges } when the mesh is not closed (repair before slicing); warnings; note in words. An object that is out of date (its body changed since it was textured) is never "ok": verdict "check", outOfDate true, and the figures mix the body's change with the texture — texture_apply { update } first, then check again. Only an "ok" goes to the slicer. It tessellates the body and measures every vertex of the mesh, so a result near the 750 000-triangle default takes a while; nothing is changed.
